newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Russia's Primakov says Washington meeting useful.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov says Washington meeting useful.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, after talks with King Hassan in Rabat, said on Monday the expected Arafat-Netanyahu meeting in Washington would be useful if U.N. peace resolutions were respected.
Primakov met King Hassan on Sunday for more than one hour at the royal palace of Skhirat on the Atlantic coast, 20 km (12 miles) south of Rabat.

That meeting came just hours after U.S. President Bill Clinton invited Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to talks in Washington this week after violence between Israelis and Palestinians in which nearly 70 people died.

"I had an interesting meeting with his majesty King Hassan...We discussed the situation in the Middle East. It is very important for us to know his opinion on the issue," Primakov told reporters before he flew back to Moscow.
Asked about the expected Israeli-Palestinian meeting in Washington, Primakov said:
"If the Israeli-Palestinian meeting takes place in line with U.N. resolutions, it would be useful."
But Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak have not yet accepted Clinton's invitation for the summit, planned for Tuesday and Wednesday.

Mubarak and Arafat have been reluctant to go, on suspicion that Clinton and Netanyahu will not give the Arabs credible guarantees that Israel will carry out old agreements and close a tunnel opened by Israel last week near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, which sparked Arab-Israeli unrest.
Primakov "exchanged points of views" with the king who holds the presidency of both the Organisation of Islamic Conference and Jerusalem Committee.
The Russian minister earlier hailed the U.N. Security Council vote calling for the immediate resumption of the Middle East peace process.

The resolution, with the backing of the 14 other Security Council members, called for the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be ensured and for the immediate resumption of the Middle East peace process.
